html:
Kuk Swamp, in the Wahgi Valley of the New Guinea Highlands, shows farming invented on its own: planting mounds from about 7,000 years ago, and drained ditch gardens by about 4,000 years ago.

Highlanders tended bananas, taro and yams in the swamp edges. New Guinea is one of the few places on Earth where farming was invented, not borrowed, like the Fertile Crescent or Mesoamerica.

Bananas domesticated in New Guinea later spread through Southeast Asia to Africa and the world. The Highlands stayed densely farmed, and the later arrival of the sweet potato let populations grow further. The valley was unknown to outsiders until the 1930s.
